solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Animal that may prowl around — it is silent

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a cat is the animal known for prowling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that some creature on the prowl is lurking out there in eerie quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' reads as describing where the animal prowls, but it turns the animal backwards before IT is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being spoken, so it is a synonym for silent in the sense of unvoiced agreement.

clue.text: The first items of toiletries everybody always leaves in a bag?

indicators.note: the first items of each word are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone always forgets their toiletries when packing a bag, leaving them behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about forgetting things; here it is the noun, the dried leaves sealed inside a teabag.
explanation.definitionFit: A teabag holds dried tea leaves, so the question-marked phrase is a playful description of the brew's ingredient.

clue.text: Dishonourably discharged head cries out

indicators.note: something out of order or out of place is disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A disgraced officer is thrown out while the commander shouts loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cries out' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'out' splits off to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them from the armed forces in disgrace, a formal military term.

clue.text: Trunk fastens in the middle… ish

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the fourth of seven letters sits at the centre
the suffix -ish means approximately, as does the phrase 'or so'

explanation.surface: A suitcase or trunk that only roughly closes at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage being fastened, but it means the body; '-ish' and 'or so' both mean roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of a body is the torso, the main part excluding head and limbs; a standard anatomical synonym.

clue.text: Case of wine with fine mixture

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
an olio is a hotchpotch or mixed dish

explanation.surface: A crate of wine sold with a pleasant blend of bottles inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of wine' reads as one unit, a box of bottles, but 'Case' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for documents or drawings, so the general word for a container fits.

clue.text: Tech device having enough power to block potentially harmful Trojans at the outset

indicators.note: the outset of each word is its opening letter, so those are kept
to block a gap is to sit inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: opening letters of the three words
able means having the power or capacity to do something

explanation.surface: A gadget with enough processing muscle to stop malware Trojans before they get in.
explanation.walkthrough: The security vocabulary suggests antivirus software; the Trojans just supply opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A phablet is a large smartphone whose screen approaches tablet size, a portmanteau of phone and tablet.

clue.text: Understand each line involved in ascent

indicators.note: something involved in a matter is caught up inside it, so these letters sit within another word

blocks.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each
L is the usual abbreviation for line
a rise is an upward climb

explanation.surface: A climber grasping every rope used on the way up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: EA for each is a price-list abbreviation; the two short pieces go together into the climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to come to grasp or comprehend it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Rich groups of elite celebs — ones who believe in destiny

blocks.note: rich food is fat, and a fat income is a rich one
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Wealthy circles of top celebrities who think their fortunes are written in the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like it describes the celebrity set, but it is a separate word meaning plump or lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatalists hold that events are predetermined and cannot be changed, which is a belief in fate.

clue.text: Piece of really crackly material

indicators.note: a piece of something is a part cut from it, so the letters come from inside the words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A scrap of noisy, rustling fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Stretchy fabric is anything but crackly, so the surface points the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a trademark for an elastic synthetic fibre used in sportswear, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Obvious thing laptops do

blocks.note: first meaning: straightforward and easily settled, as a case
second meaning: a laptop's lid is lifted up and closed down

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: a clamshell laptop is lifted and closed many times a day.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is one so clear-cut it needs no argument, an idiom for plainly obvious.

clue.text: Country song featuring American artist at the end

indicators.note: a show featuring a guest has them within it, so letters go inside
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
US is the standard abbreviation for American
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A country-music track with a guest spot from an American singer at its close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' suggests the music genre, but 'Country' is the definition and 'song' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a nation in central Europe, so the answer is one example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Diplomat is endlessly offensive and extremely hostile

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter
the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: an offensive is an attack, here missing its last letter
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An envoy behaving rudely and with open aggression, a diplomatic disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' reads as an adjective meaning rude, but it is the noun for a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a specialist member of an embassy's staff, a junior rank in the diplomatic service.

clue.text: One opinion survey in Ohio trashed ordinary citizens

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked and jumbled, so its letters are rearranged
to be in a place is to sit inside it, so these letters go within the others

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a poll canvasses people's opinions
taken as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: A single opinion poll in an Ohio town that went badly, insulting the local people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trashed' sounds like the poll insulted the citizens; it actually scrambles the state's name around the inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is a Greek-derived phrase, often slightly sneering, for the masses or common people.

clue.text: Potential outcomes from certain cognitive biases could be off the scale

definitions.text: Potential outcomes from certain cognitive biases

indicators.note: 'could be' offers what the letters might turn into, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A psychologist warning that some mental biases can have extreme results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the scale' reads as 'extreme', but it is three words of raw letters for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The halo effect is a cognitive bias in which one good trait makes people judge a person well in unrelated ways.

clue.text: Pin back a climbing plant

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters run from the end

blocks.note: a nail is a metal pin driven into wood
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener fixing a creeper flat against a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin back' looks like one gardening action of tying a plant back; 'back' turns the pin around instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lianas are woody vines of tropical forests that climb up tree trunks toward the light.

clue.text: Slow movement of large, mythical ship

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: A big legendary vessel drifting sluggishly across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow movement' suggests a ship's progress, but it is a musical term for a section of a symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a tempo marking meaning broad and slow, and a piece in that tempo is called a largo.

clue.text: After taking place, openly declare how old you are, typically

blocks.note: an event that is on is happening
to aver is to state firmly
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: Advice that, once seated, guests normally announce their age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking place' suggests sitting down; it means happening, as a show that is on.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means usually or as a rule, an idiom for what holds true in the typical case.

clue.text: Cherished gift, almost certainly diamonds

indicators.note: almost all of something stops just short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a treat is a gift, here without its last letter
sure is used to mean certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A precious present that is very likely to be a set of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gift' is a treat, docked by 'almost', not a present to be hunted in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is valued and held dear, so both words describe a loved possession.

clue.text: Banished supporter had admitted to tending to vote Republican

indicators.note: something admitted to a place is let inside it, so these letters sit within another word

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or a body
to have a meal is to eat it, so had can mean ate
in American politics red marks Republican-leaning states

explanation.surface: A party loyalist expelled after confessing to leaning towards the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' sounds political but is a leg; 'had' is had for dinner. Red is the US colour for Republican states.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to consign someone to an inferior place or exile them, so it matches banished.

clue.text: Go tumbling over a dune

indicators.note: something tumbling rolls and falls about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to roll down a sandhill for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like the verb starting a command; it is the noun, as in 'have a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is an attempt or try, and an endeavour is likewise an effort to achieve something.

clue.text: Disgusting old book connected with chaotic spectacle

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
B is the standard abbreviation for book
to make a scene is to cause a noisy public fuss

explanation.surface: A vile antique volume linked to some riotous public show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaotic spectacle' is a scene in the sense of a noisy public fuss, not a stage setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to moral standards or repugnant, so it is a synonym for repulsive.

clue.text: Cooked on a hot plate, but not initially peppered

indicators.note: without its initial, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a griddle is a flat iron cooking plate

explanation.surface: Food grilled on a hotplate, though the pepper wasn't added first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peppered' suggests seasoning in the kitchen scene; it means shot full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppered with bullets means riddled, both describing something pierced with many small holes.

clue.text: Spirit ultimately dominates every local pub

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so each word gives its final letter

blocks.note: final letters of the three words
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: Drinking culture, in the end, rules every neighbourhood bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a drink in a pub, but it is an airy being; on British maps PH marks a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is an imaginary spirit of the air in folklore, so it is a kind of elemental spirit.

clue.text: Not so free-spirited, and less socially exuberant to begin with

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is the start, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Describing someone who has become more reserved and quieter in company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' looks like the start of a comparison; it is the definition, meaning untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not so' denies that a statement is true, which is what calling it false does.

clue.text: Dance at a bar in state of oblivion

blocks.note: first meaning: a Caribbean dance of leaning back to pass under a low pole
second meaning: a neglected, forgotten condition

explanation.surface: Someone dancing in a pub until they are blind drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; in the dance it is the horizontal pole lowered each round.
explanation.definitionFit: The dance has dancers bend under a bar, and limbo is also an uncertain, overlooked or forgotten condition.

clue.text: Fish visible in small window

indicators.note: something visible in a frame is seen inside it, so these letters sit within another word

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite
slight means small or slender

explanation.surface: A fish glimpsed through a little pane of glass, as in an aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small window' reads as one phrase, but 'small' is wordplay and 'window' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a narrow window beside a door or larger window, so it is a type of window.

clue.text: Recluse, single, in Lancaster on vacation

indicators.note: to be in something is to be inside it, so this piece goes within the other
a vacated building is emptied, so the word's inner letters go and only its ends stay

blocks.note: the first and last letters
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A solitary unmarried person spending a holiday in Lancaster, an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' suggests a holiday; it empties the city's name to its two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner prefers to be alone and avoids company, which is what a recluse does.

clue.text: Be as good as guy friend with no daughter

indicators.note: with none of something means it is absent, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: compadre is an informal word for a male friend or buddy
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A man's pal measuring up even without his daughter around.
explanation.walkthrough: Compadre, borrowed from Spanish, is a pal; take out the single D.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare with something is to be its equal, as in 'nothing compares to it', meaning nothing is as good.

clue.text: Medicine reportedly associated with our group

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: associated with means linked to, and our group is us

explanation.surface: Some drug that news reports have tied to our organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Linctus is a British word for a syrupy cough medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a soothing syrup taken for coughs, so it is a particular kind of medicine.

clue.text: Is sure, from time to time, to make a legal claim

indicators.note: something happening from time to time occurs at intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally certain enough to go to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From time to time' looks like it qualifies 'sure'; it picks every second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to bring legal proceedings against someone, so it means pursuing a claim through the courts.

clue.text: Completely lifeless toad needs shifting

indicators.note: things shifting move about out of place, so the letters change order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A motionless toad that ought to be moved along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' reads as a verb about the toad, but it is fodder; 'shifting' rearranges both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-dead is an intensified idiom for undoubtedly deceased, with stone adding emphasis as in stone-cold.

clue.text: Journey taking in good Costa?

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a ride is a trip in a vehicle or on horseback
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A trip to a Spanish holiday coast, or a coffee-chain outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Costa' suggests the Costa del Sol or Costa Coffee, a British café chain; in anatomy and botany a costa is a rib-like ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is the technical Latin term for a rib or rib-like ridge on a leaf or shell, hence the question mark.
